title: introduce-reactive-webhook-toolchain-quickstart
author: Mira Patel
description: Adds a new lightweight quickstart that demonstrates a reactive webhook-based toolchain for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows; motivation: many teams build RAG integrations that rely on HTTP tool endpoints and discover brittle behavior when tool responses are slow, partial, or non-conformant to contracts; this quickstart provides a compact local runner + proxy that: 1) exposes a schema-backed mock store for tool responses (OpenAPI-lite + JSON Schema snippets), 2) demonstrates reactive backpressure handling for streaming model output while tools are resolving, 3) includes a small GraphQL gateway adapter showing how to convert webhook tool calls to typed queries and surface structured tool results back to the agent; what is included: a devcontainer + node-based local proxy (src/proxy), a sample tool mock registry (mocks/schema-registry.yaml), an example RAG agent manifest that uses tool contracts (examples/agent.yaml), a stepwise smoke test harness (tests/smoke-run.sh) and a minimal telemetry probe that records call latency and contract violations (telemetry/probes.yaml); usage: checkout, open the devcontainer, run ./dev.sh to start proxy and mock store, run the example client to see progressive streaming responses while the proxy returns delayed tool responses; checklist: [x] devcontainer and README walkthrough, [x] typed tool contract examples, [x] smoke harness + CI job, [x] telemetry probes + dashboard sample, [x] compact GraphQL adapter; compatibility notes: designed to work with Redwood SDK TS (v0.9+) and local hosted runtime; recommended for teams building webhook-oriented RAG connectors and for doc preview in the quickstarts gallery; security: mocks run only in dev mode and logging redacts secrets by default; related work: ENG-2243 tracks router-level backpressure features and ART-56 references contract linter; testing: included unit tests for contract validation and an E2E smoke that runs in GH Actions with a small Node image; follow-ups: propose an added quickstart for GRPC-based tool adapters and a chef-plate guide that maps schema violations to rollback strategies.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial scaffold with devcontainer and proxy (Mira), add schema-backed mock store and sample tools, add GraphQL adapter and agent manifest, add telemetry probe and smoke tests, update README and CI workflow;
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice focused quickstart — can we make the smoke test run with Node 18? I saw the GH Actions runner uses 20. Author: updated CI to matrix 18/20 and kept Node 20 for matrix, pushed fix.
Anya Cho: Telemetry looks useful; please add an example Grafana panel snippet. Author: added telemetry/probes.yaml and a sample panel JSON in README.
Liam Nguyen: Contract schema looks permissive; please tighten example and add a test asserting schema failure on malformed tool responses. Author: added tests/contract-failure.test.ts and CI step.
Reviewer: approved and requested squash merge once CI passes.
release_notes: Add reactive webhook toolchain quickstart: local proxy + schema-backed mocks, GraphQL adapter example, telemetry probes, and smoke CI for progressive streaming RAG scenarios.
notes_for_changelog: This quickstart helps teams validate tool contracts and observe streaming behavior when tool responses are delayed; no API changes to Redwood platform.
testing_instructions: Follow README steps in the quickstart: open devcontainer, run ./dev.sh, then node examples/client.js; run tests via npm test; CI smoke runs automatically on push.
